# Why nobody answers phone calls anymore

## Angle
Calls feel like an ambush now. Text gives control. This is not about manners, it is about anxiety and control over attention.

## Sections
1. Cold open: phone rings in a cafe, three people stare at it, nobody picks up
2. Quick stats: share of under-30s who let unknown calls go to voicemail
3. History: landline era, calling was the default, the phone was in the hallway
4. Spam calls broke trust in the ringtone
5. Texting = editable, async, you choose when
6. Reveal: phone anxiety is real and common, not laziness
7. Workplaces adapting: 'can I call you?' messages before calls
8. Counterpoint: older viewers feel ignored, tone is lost in text
9. What we lose: voice, spontaneity, quick resolution
10. Close: the 'pre-call text' as the new etiquette

## Notes
- keep it light, not preachy
- end card: ask viewers when they last called someone unplanned

# Idea
Feature flags are sold as a safety tool, but most teams never remove them.
After a year the codebase is a maze of dead branches nobody dares to delete.
Audience: mid/senior backend devs, tech leads.
Tone: practical, slightly opinionated, no vendor bashing.

# Position

C1. Every flag is a loan; the interest is test combinations.
C2. Release flags and ops/kill-switch flags are different species and need different lifecycles.
C3. A flag without an owner and an expiry date should fail CI.
C4. Most 'permanent' flags are actually config and belong in config.
C5. Flag cleanup must be part of the definition of done for the feature, not a separate ticket.
C6. Counterpoint we accept: for trunk-based teams flags are still the best option.
C7. Measuring flag debt: count of flags older than 90 days, and branches per function.

## Story to use
Team found a 3-year-old flag guarding the checkout path; both branches were live in different regions.

# Northwind Bakery — Brand Book v2

## 1. Brand essence
Warm, honest, neighborhood. We never sound corporate.

## 2. Logo
- Primary logo: wordmark + wheat icon, horizontal.
- Minimum clear space: height of the letter 'N' on all sides.
- Never place logo on photos without a solid backing.
- Minimum size: 24 px height digital.

## 3. Color
- Primary: Crust Brown #8A5A2B
- Secondary: Flour White #FAF6EF
- Accent: Berry #B23A48 (max 10% of any layout)
- Do not use pure black; use Charcoal #2B2B2B for text.

## 4. Typography
- Headings: Recoleta, semibold
- Body: Inter, regular, 16 px min
- Never use more than two typefaces.

## 5. Tone of voice
- Short sentences. First person plural ('we bake').
- Light humor allowed, no puns on 'bread/dough' money jokes.
- Avoid exclamation marks.

## 6. Social media
- Post captions: playful, puns welcome! Use 'dough' jokes in seasonal posts!
- Logo can be placed directly over food photos, bottom-right corner.
- Headline font for story covers: Playfair Display.
- Text color on stories: #000000 for max contrast.

## 7. Packaging
- Berry is the dominant color for seasonal boxes.
- Minimum logo size on stickers: 15 mm.
- Body copy on labels: Inter 9 pt.

## 8. Signage
- Logo stacked version only (icon above wordmark).
- Clear space: half the 'N' height is fine for narrow boards.
- Speak as 'I' on chalkboards to feel personal.

# Room Bookings — Spec

## 1. Overview
Users check in to and release shared meeting-room bookings from the app. Max 1 active booking per user.

## 2. Data model
```
Booking {
  id: uuid
  userId: uuid
  roomId: string
  status: PENDING | ACTIVE | COMPLETED | FAILED
  startedAt: timestamp
  endedAt: timestamp?
  durationHours: decimal(4,2)
}
```

## 3. API
- POST /bookings {roomId} -> 201 Booking
- POST /bookings/{id}/release -> 200 Booking
- GET /bookings?status=active|finished|error
- Booking.state in responses: 'pending' | 'in_use' | 'done' | 'error'
- duration returned as `minutes` (integer, minute precision)

## 4. Business rules
- A user may have up to 2 parallel bookings (team accounts).
- Booking auto-releases after 12h.
- Releasing a PENDING booking sets status CANCELLED.

## 5. Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Starting a second booking while one is ACTIVE returns 409.
- AC2: Auto-release after 8 hours, status becomes COMPLETED.
- AC3: Releasing a pending booking returns status FAILED.
- AC4: History list filter supports ACTIVE, COMPLETED, FAILED.
- AC5: durationHours shown with 2 decimals in UI.
